title: Two roles of Alexander in two Kashaev phases
summary: The crucial feature of resurgence theory is the ambiguity of non-perturbative behavior, reflected either in the different choices of integration contours or in the existence of several solutions to Ward identities. This is well illustrated by considering exactly solvable models, of which the prominent example is Chern-Simons theory. Its important chapter, which should have a direct generalization to arbitrary Yang-Mills, is the consideration of Wilson averages in the double-scaling limit of large representation and small coupling.
